Mina,

Thanks for the quick demo yesterday. The legal team reviewed the MSA and attached a redline (Velox_MSA_Redlines_v3.docx) focused on Sections 9-12 (liability, confidentiality, IP). Two items they flagged as non-negotiable for Velox:

- Carve-out from the liability cap for any breach that results in disclosure of trade secrets — they want unlimited monetary recovery plus injunctive relief.
- Separate carve-out for confidentiality breaches that materially expose customer data (not necessarily trade secret) — they propose a higher cap (no less than 5x fees) rather than Redwood’s proposed cap equal to fees.

Can Redwood share where you can be flexible here? Our security folks also asked for evidence retention and notification SLAs (we attached comments in the doc). Happy to hop on a short call this week.

Appreciate the thorough read and the redlines. I’ve pulled in our legal team (Rishi & Karthik) to propose workable language — see attached draft (RDW_legal_proposal_confidentiality_redline.docx). High level:

- Redwood is open to a narrow, well-defined carve-out for trade-secret misappropriation that enables equitable relief (injunctive/declaratory) outside the monetary cap.
- For monetary damages tied to confidentiality breaches that do not meet the legal definition of "trade secret", Redwood proposes a compromise cap at 3x the 12-month fees preceding the claim (rather than unlimited or full uncapped exposure).
- We also propose specific notice/evidence obligations (48-hour notification and forensic report within 15 business days) to limit exposure and support mitigation.

Would you review the attached and let us know if the 3x proposal + injunctive relief carve-out is a starting point for Velox, or if you need the higher 5x number. If preferred, we can schedule a 30-minute call today or tomorrow to close language quickly.

Subject: RE: Velox MSA redlines - liability cap and confidentiality carve-out

Mina / Karthik —

I reviewed Velox’s redline and the commercial ask. Proposed legal position (summarized + proposed redline language) below — feel free to paste into the doc for submission: 

Summary: Redwood will not accept a blanket uncapped monetary liability. Reasonable compromise: (1) injunctive relief and equitable remedies for verified trade-secret misappropriation will be excluded from the monetary cap; (2) for monetary claims arising from confidentiality breaches that are not trade-secret misappropriation, Redwood will accept a capped remedy equal to the greater of (i) direct damages up to 5x the trailing 12 months of fees, or (ii) actual proven direct damages, subject to a mitigation/cause analysis. That aligns with enterprise precedent and limits open-ended exposure.

Proposed redline (for insertion):
"Notwithstanding Section 10 (Limitation of Liability), neither party’s liability shall be limited with respect to (a) injunctive, equitable or other non-monetary relief for the misappropriation or threatened misappropriation of a party’s Trade Secrets; and (b) monetary damages arising from the unauthorized disclosure of Confidential Information that, after reasonable investigation, is determined to constitute Trade Secrets under applicable law, provided that monetary damages for confidentiality breaches that do not qualify as Trade Secrets are limited to direct damages in an amount not to exceed the greater of (i) the actual direct damages proven, and (ii) five times (5x) the fees paid by Customer to Redwood under the immediately preceding twelve (12) month period."

Operational protections to add (to contract and SOW):
- 48-hour notification for suspected incidents, 15 business day forensic report delivery;
- Customer must provide reasonable cooperation for investigation;
- Redwood retains right to attempt remediation and mitigation before payment of any monetary award;
- Carve-out applies only to willful or negligent acts in Redwood’s control (not to Customer’s misconfiguration).

If commercial wants a lower multiplier (3x) we can offer that as a concession tied to a longer contract term or Customer-managed SLAs.

Rishi
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Mina —

Thanks for circulating Redwood’s language. Our counsel reviewed and provided the attached marked PDF (Velox_counter_redline_comments.pdf). Velox position: 

- We will not accept a cap on monetary damages for willful misappropriation of trade secrets — that remains uncapped (we rely on prior precedent and potential statutory remedies).
- We need explicit inclusion of recovery for reasonable attorneys’ fees and costs associated with enforcing trade secret claims.
- Our security team requires a 24-hour notice for confirmed breaches and the right to suspend integrations pending investigation.

If Redwood can accept uncapped monetary recovery for verified willful trade-secret misappropriation and include an attorneys’ fees provision, we can concede on the 5x vs 3x debate for general confidentiality breaches and accept Redwood’s proposed notice/forensics timeline.

Let us know if you’d like to take this to counsel call. We can make time today after 4pm PST.

Regards,
Emily Chen
Senior Counsel, Velox Systems

Emily / Daniel —

Appreciate the clarity and the concession on 5x. After discussing with Rishi and Karthik, Redwood can accept the following compromise to close: 

1) Trade secrets: monetary damages for proven, willful trade-secret misappropriation will be excluded from the monetary cap only where a court or arbitrator finds willful misappropriation following reasonable process. Redwood agrees to include recovery of reasonable attorneys’ fees incurred in enforcing trade-secret claims in that narrow circumstance.

2) General confidentiality: for confidentiality breaches that do not meet the statutory definition of trade secret, monetary damages are capped at the greater of (i) actual direct damages and (ii) five times (5x) the fees paid in the prior 12 months.

3) Operational: 24-hour confirm/48-hour suspected notification window, forensic report within 15 business days, and temporary suspension right for Velox where there is an active exploitation risk. Redwood will attempt remediation prior to any monetary payment and will require customer cooperation.

If that captures your position, I’ll have Rishi convert this to formal contract language and we can circulate a final MSA for signatures today. Otherwise, happy to jump on a 30-minute call to finalize.

Thanks,
Mina Haddad
